films.title: SALT
films.subtitle: In 1930, the British Raj taxed the one thing every Indian could gather for free. One man picked up a handful of salt, and the Empire discovered a weapon it could not arrest.

films.title: What the Vatican Archives Actually Hide
films.subtitle: What the Vatican Archives Actually Hide. The claim that the archives are open and transparent is contested by historians who point to the selective release of documents regarding the Holocaust and modern scandals.

films.title: The Emergency
films.subtitle: The Emergency. A democracy suspended in the name of stability; the debate over civil liberty, federalism and memory remains live.

films.title: BHOPAL
films.subtitle: A pesticide plant vented methyl isocyanate over Bhopal at midnight. The gas lasted one night; the argument over who counted has lasted four decades.

films.title: Jallianwala Bagh
films.subtitle: A walled garden, a banned meeting, and a general who decided the Empire's authority was worth more than the people in front of him.
films.logline: The film is built from objects: a typed notice, a wall, a stopped watch, a well, a report, a flame. It never reconstructs the killing.
